meta.title: GitProfile Manager · The right Git identity in every repository
meta.description: Free Windows app that makes Git use the right name, email, SSH key, HTTPS account and signature in every repository, on its own.

nav.theme: Switch between light and dark mode

hero.eyebrow: Free and open source · Windows 10 and 11
hero.title: The right Git identity in every repository
hero.lead: Set up your personal, work and client accounts once. Git picks the right name, email, SSH key, HTTPS account and signature for each repo on its own: on the command line, in your editor and in SourceTree.
hero.shotAlt: GitProfile Manager showing four profiles and the identity of the default one

p1.title: Commits with the wrong email
p1.text: You push to the client's repo and the history shows your personal address. Or the other way round.

p2.title: Push rejected
p2.text: Git offers the SSH key from another account and the server says you don't have access.

p3.title: Credential pop-ups
p3.text: Two accounts on the same provider, and Git keeps asking which one to use, or picks the wrong one.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: No agent running in the background and no magic: the app writes standard Git configuration and Git does the rest.

s1.title: Create a profile per account
s1.text: Name and email, SSH key, HTTPS account and how commits are signed. GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps or your own server.

s2.title: Tell it where each one applies
s2.text: Repos in this folder or repos from this organization use this profile. Everything else uses your default one.

s3.title: Git applies it on its own
s3.text: On every commit, fetch and push, in existing repos too. You can close the app, or even uninstall it, and everything keeps working.

how.codeCaption: What the app writes: plain Git configuration you can read and edit by hand.

features.title: Everything an identity needs
features.lead: From the first SSH key to the last commit, with a preview before every change.

rules.title: Rules that decide for you
rules.text: A rule says “repos in this folder” or “repos from this organization” use this profile. The app warns you when two rules could clash, and tells you which one wins.
rules.alt: The rules view, with a conflict between two nested folders highlighted

diagnostics.title: Why is Git using that email?
diagnostics.text: Point it at any repo and it shows which profile applies, the value Git will actually use for each setting and the file it comes from. It spots the usual problems and fixes them for you.
diagnostics.alt: Diagnostics of a repository, with its applied profile and effective values

clone.title: Smart Clone
clone.text: Paste a repository URL and the app picks the profile, the method (SSH or HTTPS) and the folder, shows you the exact command, and tells you whether a rule will cover the new repo.
clone.alt: Smart Clone with a URL filled in and the profile picked from an organization rule

files.title: No magic, just Git configuration
files.text: Everything the app writes is standard Git and OpenSSH configuration. In your own .gitconfig and ~/.ssh/config it adds a single line each, after a backup.
files.alt: The generated files, readable Git configuration

updates.title: Always up to date
updates.text: Keeps the app and Git for Windows up to date: automatically, notify only or off. Every Git installer is verified first, and if you don't have Git yet, it installs it for you.
updates.alt: The Updates panel in Settings: Automatic mode selected, and Git for Windows and the app up to date

ssh.title: SSH keys made easy
ssh.text: Create a key, add it to the agent, copy the public key and test the connection, from the profile.

signing.title: Signed commits
signing.text: With your SSH key or with GPG, so your commits get the Verified badge.

https.title: HTTPS without passwords in the app
https.text: Sign-ins go through Git Credential Manager and live in Windows Credential Manager.

preview.title: See it before it happens
preview.text: Every save shows the exact diff or command first. Nothing is written until you confirm.

backups.title: Backups of every change
backups.text: Dated backups of your files, restorable in one click from Settings.

sourcetree.title: Plays well with SourceTree
sourcetree.text: It detects SourceTree's settings and tells you what to change so it uses your profiles too.

q1.q: Does it change my global Git configuration?
q1.a: Barely. It adds one include line to your .gitconfig and one to ~/.ssh/config, after a backup. Everything else lives in its own files. Your global name and email are only touched if you choose to in the first-run wizard, and they're saved first.

q2.q: Does the app need to stay open?
q2.a: No. Git reads the configuration the app wrote, so the app is only for setting things up. It doesn't start with Windows.

q3.q: Will it delete or change my SSH keys?
q3.a: Never. It can create new keys and fix the permissions of an existing one if you ask it to, but it never deletes keys, not even when you remove the app.

q4.q: Windows says “Windows protected your PC”. Is it safe?
q4.a: The installer isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info → Run anyway. The source code is public and every installer is built on GitHub from it.

q5.q: What do I need to install first?
q5.a: Windows 10 (22H2) or Windows 11, and Git for Windows 2.36 or later, which includes Git Credential Manager. If you don't have Git, the app can install it for you. The installer is per user and doesn't need administrator rights.

q6.q: Does it work on macOS or Linux?
q6.a: No, it's Windows-only: it relies on the Windows SSH agent, Windows Credential Manager and Windows file permissions.

q7.q: Does the app connect to the internet?
q7.a: For two things. When it opens, it asks GitHub for the latest versions of Git for Windows and of the app, unless updates are off. It also tests each profile's SSH and HTTPS connection against your Git provider, the same way Git connects. Your keys and passwords never leave your PC.

cta.title: Stop thinking about which account you're using
cta.text: Free, open source and installed in a minute.
